source: The Solar System master prompt (docs/SOLAR-SYSTEM.md), sections 1.8 (moves), 1.15 (quick wins) and the moon tracks of 1.10.
confidenceNote: The dollar figures behind quick wins are either a metric of the household (the honest case) or a stated convention from conventions, each an order of magnitude with its basis named, never a finding. A quick win priced on a convention says "about".
note: A move belongs to one moon and, through it, one planet; band is the band whose quick-win coverage it provides (every band on every planet has at least one quickWin, lint). dollars is an expression evaluated to cents a year: "$metricId", {"*": ["$metricId", k]} or {"convention": key}. Every level's nextMove is a move id here (lint). No string here matches the FI Skill Tree (data/skill_tree.json), lint.

missedEnrollmentMonth.what: one month of a marketplace premium bought in a hurry
missedEnrollmentMonth.source: Order of magnitude for a benchmark silver premium; the marketplace quote at Expenses 23 replaces it.

hsaTaxSavingTypical.what: a year of HSA contributions at a 22% marginal rate
hsaTaxSavingTypical.source: data/irs_limits_2026.json hsaSelfOnly times a mid bracket; the marginal bracket at Taxes 10 replaces the rate.

acaSubsidyTypicalYear.what: a year of marketplace subsidy at a modest FI income
acaSubsidyTypicalYear.source: Order of magnitude; data/aca_2026.json and the quote at Expenses 29 replace it.

tuitionBenefitTypical.what: the tax-free employer education benefit a year
tuitionBenefitTypical.source: The section 127 exclusion as commonly cited; verify against the current-year table before relying on it.

oopMaxTypical.what: an individual out-of-pocket maximum, order of magnitude
oopMaxTypical.source: The marketplace maximum as commonly cited; the plan summary at Expenses 22 replaces it.

moneyDateDriftAvoided.what: a year of small drift two people catch monthly
moneyDateDriftAvoided.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

hsaReceiptsTypical.what: a year of medical receipts reimbursable tax free later
hsaReceiptsTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

esppDiscountTypical.what: a 15% discount on a modest ESPP contribution, sold at purchase
esppDiscountTypical.source: A stated convention; Income 26 replaces it with the plan's discount.

seBookkeepingSaved.what: a year of missed deductions found with separate books
seBookkeepingSaved.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

soloRetirementTaxSaved.what: tax on a Solo 401(k) contribution at a mid bracket
soloRetirementTaxSaved.source: A stated convention; the bracket at Taxes 10 and the limit table replace it.

shopOneBillTypical.what: a year saved shopping one insurance, phone or internet bill
shopOneBillTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

cancelOneSubscriptionTypical.what: a year of one forgotten subscription
cancelOneSubscriptionTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

buyUsedTypical.what: the gap between new and used on one purchase
buyUsedTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

lateFeeAvoided.what: a year of late fees and penalty interest avoided
lateFeeAvoided.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

missingAccountTaxSaved.what: tax saved on a year of contributions to an account not yet open
missingAccountTaxSaved.source: A stated convention; the bracket and the limit table replace it.

scoreBandLoanSaving.what: a year of interest between two credit bands on a car loan
scoreBandLoanSaving.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

reportErrorTypical.what: a year of interest a corrected report error saves
reportErrorTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

utilizationRateSaving.what: a year of interest from a better rate at lower utilization
utilizationRateSaving.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

underpaymentPenaltyTypical.source: A stated convention; data/se_tax_2026.json holds the safe harbor rules.

geoShelterSavingTypical.what: a fifth off a mid-range rent for a year
geoShelterSavingTypical.source: A stated convention; the cost-of-living table (data/col_index.json) and the geo block replace it.

flexLineTypical.what: a year of one flexible line trimmed in a hard month
flexLineTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

sinkingFundOverdraftAvoided.what: a year of overdraft and card interest a sinking fund avoids
sinkingFundOverdraftAvoided.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

closeMonthLeakFound.what: a year of leak found by closing one month against the estimate
closeMonthLeakFound.source: A stated convention; the leak rate times take-home replaces it once the engine runs.

fiLinePricedTypical.what: a year of FI spending corrected by pricing one line
fiLinePricedTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

onePointOfPayTypical.what: one point of a mid pay, a year
onePointOfPayTypical.source: A stated convention; one percent of I2 replaces it once the engine runs.

automationLeakClosed.what: a year of leak closed by an automatic transfer
automationLeakClosed.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

rentalAnalysisTypical.what: a year of negative cash flow a bad rental would cost
rentalAnalysisTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

fiIncomeLineTypical.what: a year of part-time income in FI, modest
fiIncomeLineTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

stateRateMisreadTypical.what: a year of state tax misread by a default rate
stateRateMisreadTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

rothTradSwitchTypical.what: a year of tax difference between Roth and traditional at a mid bracket
rothTradSwitchTypical.source: A stated convention; the bracket at Taxes 10 replaces it.

oneCreditTypical.source: A stated convention, not a measurement.

roundUpInterestSaved.what: a year of interest saved by rounding a payment up

moves.what: Put the date your coverage changes on the calendar
moves.why: Missing open enrollment or the age-26 date means a month with no cover, or the wrong plan for a year.
moves.first15: Find the date on the benefits page or count to your 26th birthday. Add it to the Calendar room.
moves.checkpoint: The date is on the calendar with a reminder a month before.

moves.what: Check whether your plan is HSA-eligible
moves.why: An HSA is the one account that is never taxed. Only a high-deductible plan opens it.
moves.first15: Look for the words high-deductible or HSA on your plan card or summary.
moves.checkpoint: You know whether the HSA levels apply to you.

moves.what: Price a marketplace plan at your income, once
moves.why: Knowing what cover costs without a job is the number every job-loss plan needs.
moves.first15: healthcare.gov, see plans, enter your ZIP and income. Note the cheapest silver.
moves.checkpoint: A monthly premium figure is in Expenses 23.

moves.what: Compare the two plans at open enrollment: premium plus deductible against the HSA plan
moves.why: The cheaper plan on paper is often the dearer one in a bad year; the comparison takes ten minutes once a year.
moves.first15: Two plans, two figures each: the premium for the year and the deductible. Add them.
moves.checkpoint: You know which plan wins in a normal year and in a bad one.

moves.what: Check the tuition or certification benefit at work
moves.why: Many employers pay for a course or a degree and few people ask.
moves.first15: Search the benefits portal for tuition, education or learning.
moves.checkpoint: You know the yearly amount, or that there is none.

moves.what: Price the same life in one cheaper place
moves.why: Shelter is the biggest line; the same life elsewhere can move the FI date by years.
moves.first15: Pick one place. Look up a rent for the same bedrooms. Put it in the geo block.
moves.checkpoint: A geo block shows the FI date in that place.

moves.what: Write down your out-of-pocket maximum
moves.why: It is the true worst-case medical bill for a year, and the first thing a cushion must cover.
moves.first15: The plan summary, page one. Copy the individual and family figures.

moves.what: Set a monthly money date
moves.why: Twenty minutes a month keeps two people on one plan and catches drift early.
moves.first15: Pick a day. Put it on the calendar. Agenda: what moved, what is next.
moves.checkpoint: The date is on the calendar, repeating.

moves.what: Start saving medical receipts
moves.why: If the HSA is invested, receipts can be reimbursed years later, tax free.
moves.first15: Make one folder. Photograph the last receipt.
moves.checkpoint: A folder exists with one receipt in it.

moves.what: Price what a roommate, a house hack or a remote move would save you
moves.why: Flexibility is worth a number, and the number is usually the biggest line.
moves.first15: Three figures: the rent with a roommate, with a rented room, in the cheaper place.
moves.checkpoint: The shelter analysis shows the three deltas.

moves.what: See what one raise is worth over a career
moves.why: A raise is not a year of money. Invested, it compounds to the FI date.
moves.first15: Open the market pay gap. Multiply by the wealth multiplier for your age.
moves.checkpoint: You have the lifetime figure and a reason to ask.

moves.what: Get a real quote for cover before 65
moves.why: Healthcare is the biggest unknown in early retirement in the US. One quote replaces a guess.
moves.first15: Marketplace quote at the income you plan to show in FI. Note the premium and the subsidy.

moves.what: Close one coverage gap
moves.why: The cheapest cover is the one bought before it is needed.
moves.first15: Pick the first gap on the protection view. Get one quote.

moves.what: Name a beneficiary on every account
moves.why: A named beneficiary skips probate; an unnamed one goes to a court.
moves.first15: The profile page of each account, ten minutes for all of them.

moves.what: Find out the remote-work policy in writing
moves.why: Location freedom is only real when it is in the handbook.
moves.first15: Search the handbook or ask HR.
moves.checkpoint: You 27 says remote yes or no from the policy, not a hope.

moves.what: Add the move as a block
moves.why: A block shows the FI date with and without the move, side by side.
moves.first15: What-if Life, add a geo block, pick the place.
moves.checkpoint: The block is on the scenario list.

moves.what: Compare state tax at the destination
moves.why: A move can change take-home by a bracket.
moves.first15: Taxes 27 shows the delta once the destination is named.
moves.checkpoint: The tax effect of the move is on record.

moves.what: Add the kid as a block
moves.why: Childcare is a second rent for five years. Seeing it early moves the date honestly.
moves.first15: What-if Life, add a kid block, pick the year.
moves.checkpoint: The block is on the scenario list.

moves.what: Open a 529 if college is the intent
moves.why: Some states give a deduction on the way in; growth is untaxed for school.
moves.first15: Your state's plan site. Ten minutes to open.
moves.checkpoint: An account exists with an automatic monthly amount.

moves.what: Name a guardian in a will
moves.why: The one estate step that matters most with kids.
moves.first15: A simple will service or a lawyer. Name the guardian first.

moves.what: Open a custodial Roth for a kid with earned income
moves.why: Decades of tax-free growth on a summer job.
moves.first15: The brokerage's custodial Roth page. Contributions up to what the kid earned.

moves.what: Capture the whole match
moves.why: It is the only guaranteed 50 to 100% return anywhere.
moves.first15: Open the retirement plan portal. Set the contribution to the percent the match needs.

moves.what: Take the ESPP discount and sell on a schedule
moves.why: A 15% discount on stock you sell the day it lands is a 15% raise on that money.
moves.first15: Enroll in the ESPP at the max you can carry. Set a rule: sell at purchase.
moves.checkpoint: Enrollment is on, with a sell rule written down.

moves.what: Price one hour of your skill
moves.why: Knowing what an hour sells for turns a vague idea into a number.
moves.first15: Find three people selling the same skill. Note their rate.
moves.checkpoint: A rate per hour is in the moon intake.

moves.what: Update the resume and one profile
moves.why: Being findable costs nothing and is how most raises arrive.
moves.first15: One page, current title, three results with numbers.
moves.checkpoint: The file is dated this month.

moves.what: Add a job change as a block
moves.why: A 20% jump and its effect on the date, without doing anything yet.
moves.first15: What-if Life, job change block, the market rate.
moves.checkpoint: The block is on the list.

moves.what: Ask for the market rate
moves.why: The market pay gap is the biggest single lever most people never pull.
moves.first15: Book the conversation. Bring the three postings.
moves.checkpoint: A date is set for the conversation.

moves.what: Track side income net of costs for one month
moves.why: Gross flatters. Net after costs and hours is the real wage.
moves.first15: One sheet: money in, money out, hours.

moves.what: Separate the business account
moves.why: One account per entity makes taxes and a bad year survivable.
moves.first15: Open a business checking account. Move the next payment there.
moves.checkpoint: Business money lands in its own account.

moves.what: Open a Solo 401(k) or SEP IRA
moves.why: Self-employment income can shelter far more than an IRA alone.
moves.first15: The brokerage's small-business retirement page. The limit is in the dated table.
moves.checkpoint: The account exists with one contribution.

moves.what: Plan income in FI: one line
moves.why: Part-time, rental or a pension changes the FI number more than most saving.
moves.first15: Income 29, one line, a rough monthly figure.

moves.what: List one offer somewhere
moves.why: The first dollar is the hard one.
moves.first15: One platform, one listing, one price.

moves.what: Shelter the side income in a retirement account
moves.why: Side income can go into a Solo 401(k) or SEP.
moves.first15: Same page as the business version.

moves.what: Set the four quarterly tax reminders
moves.why: The safe harbor keeps a penalty away; the reminders keep the safe harbor.
moves.first15: Calendar, four dates from the tax table.

moves.what: Price your time as the business sees it
moves.why: A business that pays you less than a job is a hobby with paperwork.
moves.first15: Revenue minus costs, over hours.
moves.checkpoint: Income 18 shows the business hourly figure.

moves.what: Shop one bill
moves.why: Insurance, phone and internet drift up every year for people who do not call.
moves.first15: Pick the bill you have not shopped in two years. Get one competing quote.
moves.checkpoint: A quote is in hand, or the bill is lower.

moves.what: Cancel one subscription
moves.why: A subscription you forgot costs 300 times its monthly price in FI number.
moves.first15: Scroll one statement for a name you do not recognize. Cancel it.
moves.checkpoint: One line is gone from Expenses 7.

moves.what: Price the next big purchase used
moves.why: The same thing used is usually half, and the difference compounds.
moves.first15: Look the item up second-hand. Note the gap.
moves.checkpoint: The gap is written on the purchase in Big Purchase.

moves.what: Flag which lines could flex
moves.why: Knowing what can drop in a bad month is what makes a cushion small enough to fund.
moves.first15: Expenses 10, one tap per line.

moves.what: Set up sinking funds
moves.why: Irregular costs stop being surprises when they are saved for monthly.
moves.first15: One savings bucket per irregular cost, or one with a note. Set the monthly amount from the targets.

moves.what: Set autopay to the full balance
moves.why: Rewards only count when no interest is paid. Autopay makes that automatic.
moves.first15: The card app, autopay, statement balance.

moves.what: Close one month in the Budget room
moves.why: The estimate meets the actual, and the gap between them is the leak made visible.
moves.first15: Budget room, close the month, read the divergence.

moves.what: Price the shock costs once
moves.why: COBRA, a move, a car: knowing the figures turns a fear into a line.
moves.first15: Expenses 23: the COBRA rate is on the benefits page; a move and a car are one search each.

moves.what: Point the right card at the spending you already do
moves.why: Two percent back on what you were buying anyway is free money with no new spending.
moves.first15: Check which card pays most on groceries and fuel. Use it there.
moves.checkpoint: Rewards value per year is up.

moves.what: Price one line of FI spending
moves.why: What drops and what rises in FI decides the number more than any return assumption.
moves.first15: Expenses 28, fix one guessed line.
moves.checkpoint: One line in Expenses 28 is yours, not the app's guess.

moves.what: Check the annual fee math
moves.why: A fee card that earns less than its fee is a subscription.
moves.first15: Rewards value on that card minus the fee.
moves.checkpoint: Every fee card has a verdict.

moves.what: One sign-up bonus on spending already planned
moves.why: A bonus on spending you would do anyway is the biggest rewards move, once the balance is zero every month.
moves.first15: Match the minimum spend to a planned purchase.

moves.what: Capture the whole match, every paycheck
moves.why: Step one of every order of operations, because it is free money.
moves.first15: Retirement plan portal, set the contribution to the match percent.

moves.what: Move the cash to a higher rate
moves.why: Cash at 0.01% is money working for the bank. A high-yield account is fifteen minutes.
moves.first15: Open a high-yield savings account. Move the emergency fund.

moves.what: Open the missing account
moves.why: The next slot for your money usually needs an account that does not exist yet.
moves.first15: The next slot names it. The brokerage opens it in ten minutes.

moves.what: Raise the contribution by one point
moves.why: One point is invisible in a paycheck and years on the FI date.
moves.first15: Plan portal, contribution rate, plus one.

moves.what: Automate the next slot
moves.why: What is automatic happens. What is manual happens in January.
moves.first15: Set a monthly transfer to the account the next slot names.

moves.what: Confirm the emergency fund target and stop overfilling
moves.why: Cash past the target is cash not compounding.
moves.first15: Assets 18, confirm the months. Move anything over it.

moves.what: Check the fee on the target-date fund
moves.why: Some target-date funds cost ten times an index fund for the same mix.
moves.first15: The fund page, expense ratio.

moves.what: Split the cushion: one month reachable today, the rest at the best rate
moves.why: A shock needs cash today; the rest can earn.
moves.first15: One month in checking, the rest in high-yield.
moves.checkpoint: The cushion is in two places.

moves.what: Swap the expensive fund
moves.why: Fee drag compounds against you for decades. The swap takes ten minutes.
moves.first15: Find the fund with the highest expense ratio. Exchange it for the index equivalent in the same account.

moves.what: Run the numbers on one rental
moves.why: Cap rate and cash-on-cash say in ten minutes whether a property is an investment or a hobby.
moves.first15: Assets 28, four numbers from one listing.

moves.what: Fund a starter cushion
moves.why: One month of bare-bones costs keeps a flat tire from becoming card debt.
moves.first15: A transfer to savings equal to one bare-bones month, or a monthly amount to get there.

moves.what: Clear the high-interest debt
moves.why: Nothing in the market beats paying off 24%.
moves.first15: Every spare dollar to the highest rate until it is gone.

moves.what: Collect one bank account bonus
moves.why: Banks pay to move money in. Kept separate from card rewards.
moves.first15: One bonus offer with a direct-deposit requirement you already meet.

moves.what: Run the Rule of 5
moves.why: Five layers of cushion, from the deductible up to a job loss.
moves.first15: Runway room, Rule of 5.

moves.what: Pick a three-fund mix
moves.why: Total US, total international, total bond: the whole market at the lowest fee.
moves.first15: The Mix room, three-fund template.

moves.what: Set a yearly rebalance date
moves.why: Once a year is enough. It is on the annual review.
moves.first15: Calendar, one date.

moves.what: Run the house hack
moves.why: Renting out one room can cut shelter by a third.
moves.first15: Housing room, house hack, one rent figure.

moves.what: Get a preapproval figure
moves.why: The lender's number and the app's capacity should agree.
moves.first15: One lender, one preapproval.

moves.what: Check whether PMI can drop
moves.why: At 80% loan-to-value, conventional PMI can go.
moves.first15: Loan-to-value from Assets 6 and Debt 4. Call the servicer.
moves.checkpoint: PMI is off, or the date it can be.

moves.what: Run rent versus buy
moves.why: Five percent of the price a year is the unrecoverable cost to beat.
moves.first15: Housing room, rent versus buy.

moves.what: Cap alternatives at a share
moves.why: A small share cannot sink the plan; a large one can.
moves.first15: Pick a cap. Write it in the leverage policy.

moves.what: Check I-bonds for part of the cushion
moves.why: Inflation-linked, government-backed, after the first year.
moves.first15: treasurydirect.gov.

moves.what: List every alternative you hold
moves.why: Crypto and collectibles are net worth too, at the value you would get.
moves.first15: Assets 9, one line each.

moves.what: Check your score for free
moves.why: Most bank and card apps show it. Knowing the band opens the credit reads.
moves.first15: The bank app, credit score.

moves.what: Set every minimum to autopay
moves.why: One late payment costs more score than a year of good ones.
moves.first15: Each lender, autopay, at least the minimum.

moves.what: Pick your payoff order
moves.why: Avalanche saves the most interest; snowball wins the most months. Either beats no order.
moves.first15: Debt Payoff room. Read both columns. Tap one.

moves.what: Call for a lower rate
moves.why: A ten-minute call often takes points off a card rate for a good payer.
moves.first15: Call the number on the card. Ask for a rate reduction. Mention a competing offer.
moves.checkpoint: Debt 7 has a lower rate, or a no.

moves.what: Automate the extra payment
moves.why: Extra that is automatic arrives every month. Extra that is manual arrives some months.
moves.first15: Set a recurring extra payment to the target debt.

moves.what: Handle the promo expiry before it lands
moves.why: A 0% balance at 27% the next day is the promo cliff.
moves.first15: Calendar the end date. Plan the balance to zero, or a transfer, before it.
moves.checkpoint: The promo cliff is on the calendar with a plan.

moves.what: Pull the free credit report
moves.why: Errors are common and cost points. The pull is free and takes ten minutes.
moves.first15: annualcreditreport.com, all three.

moves.what: Pay one card before the statement date
moves.why: Utilization is read on the statement date. Paying before it lowers the reported number.
moves.first15: Pick the card with the highest balance. Pay it a few days before the statement closes.

moves.what: Dispute one error
moves.why: A disputed error is usually removed within a month.
moves.first15: The bureau's dispute page, one item.

moves.what: Get one refinance quote
moves.why: A better band since the loan was written is a lower rate waiting to be asked for.
moves.first15: One lender, one quote, for the largest loan.

moves.what: Round the payment up
moves.why: A round number on top of a minimum saves interest for the life of the loan.
moves.first15: Change the autopay amount to the next round hundred.
moves.checkpoint: Interest saved per extra dollar shows.

moves.what: Freeze your credit
moves.why: Free, reversible, and it stops identity theft cold.
moves.first15: Each bureau, freeze. Ten minutes for all three.

moves.what: Open a secured card if there is no history
moves.why: A history starts with one small line paid in full.
moves.first15: A secured card at your bank. One small charge a month, autopay in full.

moves.what: Write the leverage policy
moves.why: Decide the rate and the purpose before the offer, not during it.
moves.first15: Debt 30, two answers.

moves.what: Stress-test the rate
moves.why: A payment at plus two points is the number to be able to afford.
moves.first15: Debt 22.

moves.what: Check debt-to-income before borrowing
moves.why: Lenders read it; so should you.
moves.first15: Debt 27.

moves.what: Check the state tax rate you are paying
moves.why: The rough rate from the state table is a default until you confirm it.
moves.first15: Taxes 1, one tap, or the stub's state line.

moves.what: Confirm the accounts you use are the tax-advantaged ones offered
moves.why: An offered account not in use is the next slot.
moves.first15: Taxes 5, one tap.

moves.what: Fix your withholding
moves.why: A big refund is an interest-free loan to the government. Owing a lot is a bill in April.
moves.first15: Payroll portal, W-4. Use the IRS estimator for the numbers.
moves.checkpoint: Projected refund or owed is near zero.

moves.what: Switch the contribution type if the call says so
moves.why: Roth or traditional is a bracket call, and the app made it.
moves.first15: Plan portal, contribution type.

moves.what: Claim one credit you were missing
moves.why: The saver's credit and the student loan interest deduction go unclaimed every year.
moves.first15: Taxes 17, tick the first unclaimed one. Tell your software or preparer.

moves.what: Put the HSA into an index fund
moves.why: An HSA sitting in cash is the best account in the code used as a checking account.
moves.first15: HSA portal, investments, pick an index fund.

moves.what: Set the quarterly estimate reminders
moves.why: Missing one is a penalty; the dates are in the table.
moves.first15: Calendar, four dates.

moves.what: File last year's return where someone can find it
moves.why: A found return is a checked bracket and a survivable audit.
moves.first15: One folder, one file, the location in Taxes 23.

moves.what: Check the safe harbor
moves.why: Paying in 100% of last year's tax keeps the penalty away whatever this year does.
moves.first15: Taxes 22.

moves.what: Harvest gains at 0% in a low-income year
moves.why: Selling and rebuying inside the 0% bracket raises the basis for free.
moves.first15: Taxes 25 shows the room. Sell and rebuy up to it.

moves.what: Map the income to show in early FI
moves.why: Landing MAGI under a cliff is worth thousands a year in subsidy.
moves.first15: Taxes 28, read the map. Note the target income.

moves.what: Do a backdoor Roth if income is over the limit
moves.why: Above the limit the front door closes; the back door is the same account.
moves.first15: Contribute to a traditional IRA, convert. Watch the pro-rata rule if a pretax IRA exists.
